The **Committee of Five** of the [Second Continental Congress](Second_Continental_Congress "Second Continental Congress") was a group of five members who drafted and presented to the full Congress in [Pennsylvania State House](Independence_Hall "Independence Hall") what would become the [United States Declaration of Independence](United_States_Declaration_of_Independence "United States Declaration of Independence") of July 4, 1776. This Declaration committee operated from June 11, 1776, until July 5, 1776, the day on which the Declaration was published.

The Committee was composed of [John Adams](John_Adams "John Adams"), [Benjamin Franklin](Benjamin_Franklin "Benjamin Franklin"), [Thomas Jefferson](Thomas_Jefferson "Thomas Jefferson"), [Robert Livingston](Robert_R._Livingston "Robert R. Livingston"), and [Roger Sherman](Roger_Sherman "Roger Sherman").

## The Committee of Five

The members of this committee were:

- [John Adams](John_Adams "John Adams"), representative of [Massachusetts](Province_of_Massachusetts_Bay "Province of Massachusetts Bay"), who later became the second president of the United States[[1]](Committee_of_Five#cite_note-1)
- [Thomas Jefferson](Thomas_Jefferson "Thomas Jefferson"), representative of [Virginia](Colony_of_Virginia "Colony of Virginia"), who later became the third president of the United States[[2]](Committee_of_Five#cite_note-2)
- [Benjamin Franklin](Benjamin_Franklin "Benjamin Franklin"), representative of [Pennsylvania](Province_of_Pennsylvania "Province of Pennsylvania"), known as one of the most famous intellectuals among the [Founding Fathers](Founding_Fathers_of_the_United_States "Founding Fathers of the United States"), whose academic writings and press publications had a very significant influence in the American Revolution, the only person to sign the [Declaration of Independence](United_States_Declaration_of_Independence "United States Declaration of Independence"), [Treaty of Alliance with France](Treaty_of_Alliance_(1778) "Treaty of Alliance (1778)"), [Treaty of Paris](Treaty_of_Paris_(1783) "Treaty of Paris (1783)"), and [U.S. Constitution](Constitution_of_the_United_States "Constitution of the United States")
- [Roger Sherman](Roger_Sherman "Roger Sherman"), representative of [Connecticut](Connecticut_Colony "Connecticut Colony"), the only person to sign all four of the U.S. state papers: the [Continental Association](Continental_Association "Continental Association"), the [Declaration](United_States_Declaration_of_Independence "United States Declaration of Independence"), the [Articles of Confederation](Articles_of_Confederation "Articles of Confederation"), and the [Constitution](United_States_Constitution "United States Constitution")[[3]](Committee_of_Five#cite_note-3)
- [Robert Livingston](Robert_R._Livingston "Robert R. Livingston"), representative of [New York](Province_of_New_York "Province of New York"), who later served as the first [United States Secretary of Foreign Affairs](United_States_Secretary_of_Foreign_Affairs "United States Secretary of Foreign Affairs"), administered the [presidential oath of office](Oath_of_office_of_the_President_of_the_United_States "Oath of office of the President of the United States") at the [First inauguration of George Washington](First_inauguration_of_George_Washington "First inauguration of George Washington") and negotiated the [Louisiana Purchase](Louisiana_Purchase "Louisiana Purchase") as the minister to France.[[4]](Committee_of_Five#cite_note-4)

The delegates of the [Thirteen Colonies](Thirteen_Colonies "Thirteen Colonies") in Congress resolved to postpone until Monday, July 1, the final consideration of whether or not to declare the several sovereign independencies of the Colonies, which had been proposed by the [North Carolina resolutions of April 12](Halifax_Resolves "Halifax Resolves") and the Virginia resolutions of May 15. The proposal, known as the [Lee Resolution](Lee_Resolution "Lee Resolution"), was moved in Congress on June 7 by [Richard Henry Lee](Richard_Henry_Lee "Richard Henry Lee") of Virginia. He is the only person to sign all four great state papers of the United States: the [Continental Association](Continental_Association "Continental Association"), the [Declaration of Independence](United_States_Declaration_of_Independence "United States Declaration of Independence"), the [Articles of Confederation](Articles_of_Confederation "Articles of Confederation"), and the [Constitution](Constitution_of_the_United_States "Constitution of the United States").[[1]](Roger_Sherman#cite_note-Roger_Sherman-1)[[2]](Roger_Sherman#cite_note-allthingsliberty.com-2) He also signed the 1774 [Petition to the King](Petition_to_the_King "Petition to the King").

Born in Newton, Massachusetts Sherman established a legal career in [Litchfield County, Connecticut](Litchfield_County%2C_Connecticut "Litchfield County, Connecticut"), despite a lack of formal education. After a period in the [Connecticut House of Representatives](Connecticut_House_of_Representatives "Connecticut House of Representatives"), he served as a justice of the Superior Court of Connecticut from 1766 to 1789. He represented Connecticut at the [Continental Congress](Continental_Congress "Continental Congress"), and he was a member of the [Committee of Five](Committee_of_Five "Committee of Five") that drafted the Declaration of Independence.
